evidence: The current architecture—a single MySQL instance behind a monolithic web app—will fail at this scale for several reasons:

Single database: All reads and writes hit one MySQL server. At ~660 peak QPS, MySQL can handle this load, but the database becomes a single point of failure and cannot scale horizontally without sharding.
No caching: Every timeline request triggers a full database query, causing high latency and database load.
Synchronous fan-out: When a user posts, the app must synchronously update all followers' timelines, which is O(followers) work per post and blocks the request.
No observability: Without metrics, logs, and tracing, you cannot diagnose performance issues or capacity bottlenecks.
No global distribution: Users outside the primary region experience high latency (e.g., 200–300 ms RTT from Asia to US-East).

Recommendation: Refactor the application to be stateless—no session state stored in memory. Use JWT (JSON Web Tokens) for authentication, storing user ID and claims in the token. This allows horizontal scaling behind a load balancer.
